To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) γTuRCs are in a closed state on microtubules, (ii) this state is a better nucleator, and (iii) γTuRC nucleates microtubules using only tubulin from the species of origin.
the ring closure of the γ-tublin ring complex is essential to activate its microtubule-nucleation function, and that the ring closure is species-specific.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function of the γ-tublin ring complex (γγTuRC), the microtubule (MT) nucleator in cells, in yeast and human.
how the γ-tubulins are organized within the γTuRC to form the ring and how this structure controls microtubule formation.
the structure and function of the γ-tubulins, the proteins that nucleate the microtubules in cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the closed state is the active state of γTuRC, and that γTuRC activity is regulated by a species-specific conformational change.
the ring closure of γTuRC is required for species-specific nucleation of microtubules.
the γTuSC ring is in a closed con-formation in the context of the yeast γTuRC and that the ring is in a conformation that precisely matches microtubl symmetry and is a stronger nucleating complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
γTuRC nucleation activity is regulated by the conformational state of γTuSCs and by their species-specificity.
γTuRC nucleation is activated by the ring closure of γTuSC and the closed state of γTuSC matches the microtubule lattice.
γTuRC is a dynamic complex with a conformational switch that controls nucleation and that this conformation can also control species specificity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the γ-tubu-lin ring is a key determinant of γTuRC function.
γTuRC is a dynamic nucleator that can adopt multiple conformations, with different conformations activating γTuRC for nucleation in different species.
the closed conformation of the γ-tubulins is essential for nucleation of microtubules in cells.
